methodological_rigor.justification: The study is fundamentally built on synthetic cohorts whose outcomes are generated from explicit logistic functions of BED (Sections 2.3, 2.6.3, 2.7.3, 2.8.3). ML models and Bayesian inference then 'recover' relationships that were hard-coded into the data generators, which is largely circular validation. The sensitivity analyses, 5-fold CV, bootstrap CIs, and univariate benchmarking (Section 3.2.6) are competent, and the inter-fraction repair sensitivity analysis is thoughtful. However, the sole real-world validation (Section 3.9) involves only 60 lesions with volume as predictor and no BED/time-structure data, so it cannot validate the mechanistic claims. No power calculation is reported, DeLong's test failed numerically, and multiplicity across 12 model comparisons (4 pathologies x 3 models) is not addressed.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is primarily a computational/simulation study with pathology-specific generators and an exploratory 60-patient retrospective check, mapping to Oxford LoE 5 (mechanistic/basic modeling). The research question of biologically optimized GKS prescription is clinically important, but the findings are entirely contingent on assumed radiobiological generators and cannot inform practice without real validation, which the authors explicitly defer. Endpoints are simulated binary outcomes without time-to-event or competing risks; the real cohort analyzes only volume vs. 1-year recurrence/survival, not AI-BED-Fx itself. The authors appropriately caveat limitations but overclaim clinical readiness in Sections 4.6 and 4.10.

reporting_quality.justification: TRIPOD is the most applicable standard given the prediction-model development across four cohorts. Methods are detailed for data generation, feature engineering, model training, and evaluation; calibration curves, confidence intervals, and SHAP interpretability are reported. However, there is no protocol registration, no explicit TRIPOD checklist, limited reporting of model specification uncertainty, and the real-cohort analysis in Section 2.12 is thin. No data or code availability statement is present in the manuscript, and the synthetic cohort generators (which are the entire basis of the work) are described but no repository or seed is provided for independent replication.

novelty_literature.justification: The explicit extension of the Jones-Hopewell biexponential repair model to multi-fraction GKS schedules (1, 3, 5 fractions) is a genuine methodological contribution, as is the pairing with ML surrogates and Bayesian alpha/beta inference. However, LQ-based multi-fraction BED computation, neural-network radiobiological surrogates (ref. 20), and ML-based outcome prediction in radiosurgery (refs. 21-23) are all documented in cited prior work. The core empirical finding (BED utility is pathology-dependent) is largely a consequence of the hand-coded generators rather than a discovery. Novelty is incremental and primarily conceptual/framework-oriented.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is readable and logically organized (Intro, Methods, Results per pathology, Discussion), with a thorough comparison section and explicit limitations. However, it is highly repetitive, with the same three-model framework and conclusions restated across four pathology sections and again in cross-pathology synthesis; the abstract is long and includes narrative paragraphs atypical of structured abstracts. Bulleted lists are over-used and some equations are poorly formatted (e.g., Eqs. 1, 7, 12). Captions and figures are referenced but table/figure numbering is sometimes decoupled from narrative, and several claims (e.g., 'first unified framework') are overstated.

key_strengths: Mechanistic extension of Jones-Hopewell biexponential repair model to 1/3/5-fraction GKS with explicit treatment-time structure
Thoughtful sensitivity analysis on inter-fraction repair carry-over (5/10/20%) and comparison to classical LQ BED (Section 3.2.6)
Rigorous ML evaluation infrastructure: stratified 75/25 split, 5-fold CV, bootstrap CIs, SHAP interpretability, surrogate MLP with R2=0.9991
Explicit acknowledgment that findings are synthetic-generator-contingent and clinical validation is pending
key_concerns: Core circularity: ML models and Bayesian inference recover BED relationships that were explicitly hard-coded into logistic data generators (Eqs. 4, 9, 10, 11); recovery is near-tautological
Only real-world data is a 60-lesion volume-only analysis that cannot validate AI-BED-Fx and is not powered for meaningful conclusions
No code/data availability, no protocol registration, no formal TRIPOD compliance despite being a prediction-model paper across four cohorts
Overclaiming: 'first unified framework', 'AI discovers radiobiology', and clinical-translation framing (Section 4.6) exceed what synthetic experiments can support
Multiple comparisons across 12 model configurations without multiplicity correction; DeLong test failed numerically; CIs are very wide (e.g., AVM AUC CI 0.75-0.995)
Pathology-specific generator parameters (alpha/beta, repair half-times) are chosen to produce the exact spectrum of behaviors the manuscript then claims to discover
chief_reviewer.rationale: The paper is a competent but largely circular simulation study with limited real-world grounding. Tier 3 (e.g., methodology or specialty radiosurgery journal) is plausible after major revisions to reframe claims around mechanistic/computational demonstration rather than discovery, add code/data availability, and either strengthen or de-emphasize the real-cohort analysis.
